title: soft-landing-priority-bands-occupancy-signals
content:
Goal:
- Capture a candidate design for admission that avoids abrupt drops and gives a predictable "soft landing" when regional capacity becomes constrained. Focus on combining token-bucket style budgets with direct occupancy signals (queue depth, GPU SM/mem pressure) and an admit probability curve rather than sharp cutoffs.

Summary of idea (one-liner):
- Replace single-threshold admit rules with priority bands and a smooth sigmoid-shaped admit probability that is driven by a weighted occupancy score and per-tenant headroom budget (token-bucket).

Key concepts / building blocks:
1) Occupancy score (local):
   - Inputs: service queue depth (Q), per-GPU compute occupancy (SM% or util), GPU memory pressure (Mem%), active KV cache size, recent p90 latency (L90).
   - Normalize each signal to 0..1 based on rolling baselines per-instance and compute a weighted sum: Occupancy = w_q*norm(Q) + w_sm*norm(SM) + w_mem*norm(Mem) + w_lat*norm(L90).
   - Weights are tunable per-region or per-instance type. Default: w_q=0.4, w_sm=0.3, w_mem=0.2, w_lat=0.1

2) Priority bands (soft lanes):
   - Fast lane (Band A): latency sensitive, small batch sizes, high cost_tier. High token burn but low tolerance to waiting.
   - Standard lane (Band B): default, balanced latency/cost.
   - Background lane (Band C): best-effort, high batching allowed, longer deadlines, lowest priority.
   - Each request carries a band hint (inferred from tenant config or API route). The routing layer may rewrite band based on observed SLAs.

3) Per-tenant headroom (regional token bucket):
   - Dedicated token buckets per tenant per-region with refill_rate = committed_capacity * safe_factor.
   - Tokens are debited on admit using an estimated token_cost = tokens_per_tokenized_input + model_multiplier.
   - If tokens depleted: admission probability for that tenant gracefully degrades via multiplier rather than hard block (unless safety mode).

4) Sigmoid admit probability function:
   - AdmitProb = S( alpha*(HeadroomMargin) - beta*(Occupancy) + gamma*(band_bias) ) where S is logistic curve.
   - HeadroomMargin derived from token bucket (normalized), Occupancy from local signals. Band_bias moves curve right/left for priority.
   - This yields a smooth decline in admits as occupancy rises. We avoid step functions that create request storms when capacity frees.

5) Cross-region spillover & fast fallback:
   - If AdmitProb drops below a secondary threshold for >T secs, control plane considers cross-region spill to regions with available headroom.
   - Spill decisions are conservative: prefer cold spares with compatible model artifact and acceptable latency multiplier.
   - Fallback rules: try model-quantized variant first (lower cost), then cross-region, then degrade band to C.

6) Local controller responsibilities (per-node):
   - Compute Occupancy using cheap in-proc probes (queue length, cudaUtil, memAvail).
   - Keep a small reservoir token estimate for immediate admits (fast-path) synchronized with control plane every ~500ms.
   - Apply AdmitProb per request; if rejected, optionally enqueue in deferred lane if deadline allows.

7) Control plane responsibilities (global):
   - Aggregate per-node occupancy and replenish/refill token budgets per-tenant-per-region.
   - Run smoothing over noisy signals (exponential moving averages with tunable half-life).
   - Compute region-level admission policies and push band_bias adjustments to nodes.

Operational metrics to expose:
- Per-band admitted QPS, rejected QPS, deferred QPS.
- Occupancy components: queue depth percentiles, GPU SM util, mem pressure.
- Token bucket utilization and refill rates per-tenant-region.
- AdmitProb distribution and decisions count by reason (headroom, occupancy, band).
- p50/p90 latency per-band and per-tenant pre/post-admit.

Dashboard ideas:
- Heatmap: region x time of Occupancy score vs admitted rate.
- Token budget burn-down widgets per-commit tier.
- Long tail analysis: which customers get deferred or downgraded most often.

Why sigmoid / probability helps:
- Smoothness avoids synchronized retries: when capacity returns, admit rate ramps up gradually instead of releasing a large queued backlog that spikes usage again.
- Allows statistical multiplexing across tenants: lower-priority requests take last-available capacity opportunistically.
- Easier to A/B test steepness (alpha) to tradeoff latency vs throughput.

Tuning knobs (experiment matrix):
- alpha (sigmoid slope) — controls how sharp the drop is around threshold.
- beta (occupancy weight) vs headroom weight — prioritization between instantaneous signals and budget.
- per-band biases — how much earlier/late each band gets throttled.
- reservoir size at node vs control plane sync interval — latency vs accuracy tradeoff.

Failure modes / safety checks:
- Control plane outage: nodes continue using local reservoir tokens for short period (grace window). If reservoir exhausted, conservative fallback to background lane only.
- Signal poisoning: implement median-of-nodes to avoid single bad probe (one node reporting zero memory causes cascade).
- Token synchronization drift: keep monotonic counters and reconcile on reconnect.

Backpressure vs queueing semantics:
- Prefer immediate admit/reject over deep queuing at node boundary unless request declares deadline > X ms. Deep queues hurt tail latency in general.
- Deferred queue: bounded, FIFO per-band, admission from deferred queue only when AdmitProb > threshold or headroom recovered.

Interactions with model variants & cost controls:
- Admit decision should consider model variant cost (e.g., 8-bit quantized variant uses fewer tokens). AdmitProb formula uses an effective cost multiplier so cheaper variants get higher chance.
- Encourage clients to surface deadline and cost_tier so routing can make better decisions.

Experiment plan (short):
- Phase 0: Simulate with historical traces (1 week window) and run offline admit sim with various alpha/beta. Measure p90 latency and dropped QPS per-tenant.
- Phase 1: Canary on single non-critical region with 5% traffic for selected tenants. Expose metrics and alert on drop in success rate > 3x baseline.
- Phase 2: Roll to additional regions and tune per-region baselines.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to compute global headroom for bursty tenants that shift region-to-region? (need per-tenant multi-region budget or global spill policy)
- How to choose default weights for occupancy components across diverse GPU types? (calibration job per-instance-type)
- Should we include request size (tokens_in prompt) in Occupancy as first-class signal? (pros and cons)
- Backpressure signalling to client SDKs: do we return a structured retry-after or a best-effort partial-response?

Immediate action items:
- (Aisha) Build offline simulator that consumes 7 days of ingest logs and runs admit-model with configurable knobs. (ETA 2w)
- (Daniel) Add light-weight CUDA util probe to node agent and expose normalized metric to control plane. (ETA 1w)
- (Marina) Draft proposal for token-cost model per-route and gather feedback from pricing/Product. (ETA 1.5w)
- (Ravi) Wire up a Grafana dashboard prototype that shows Occupancy heatmap + admit probability. (ETA 1w)

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc is intentionally a sketch: looking for feedback on the core affordance (probabilistic admit + token budget) and whether priority bands should be expanded to a continuous priority score.
- Related reading: see CONFLUENCE-PLAT-1234 for capacity accounting model and JIRA-PLT-876 for a recent incident where hard cutoffs created a retry storm.

Rough glossary (short):
- headroom: available tokens in region/tenant bucket normalized to expected burn.
- reservoir: local node short-term token estimate used for fast admits.
- AdmitProb: probability computed from control-node formula that decides admit/reject when combined with a RNG pass.

End.
